leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Holds workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is sex discrimination under Title VII; basis for employment protections in Nebraska
leads.detail: Decided June 15, 2020, consolidated with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission

leads.title: Nebraska Equal Opportunity Commission - August 2020 announcement
leads.documents: State enforcement machinery: will investigate and resolve housing discrimination claims on account of sexual orientation or gender identity in light of Bostock
leads.detail: Announced August 2020; Executive Director Marna Munn quoted: 'We will now be investigating housing claims on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity'

leads.title: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) guidance
leads.documents: Directs state/local Fair Housing Assistance Program agencies to interpret Fair Housing Act sex discrimination to include sexual orientation and gender identity
leads.detail: Issued February 11, 2021; applies in Nebraska to Nebraska Equal Opportunity Commission, Lincoln Commission on Human Rights, and Omaha Human Rights and Relations Department

leads.title: Governor Jim Pillen Executive Order defining sex - August 30, 2023
leads.documents: Defines female as reproductive system 'designed to produce ova' and male as 'designed to fertilize the ova'; stated intent to provide single-sex spaces for women's sports, bathrooms, and changing rooms
leads.detail: Signed August 30, 2023 by Governor Jim Pillen

leads.title: Legislative Bill 89 - female protection in sports bill
leads.documents: Explicitly bans transgender athletes from any sports within Nebraska
leads.detail: Signed June 2025 by Governor Jim Pillen; passed unicameral Nebraska Legislature by two-thirds majority; LGBTQ Nation identified 10 transgender athletes affected

leads.title: Nebraska gender-affirming healthcare ban on under age 19 and Nebraska Supreme Court ruling July 2024
leads.documents: Bans gender-affirming healthcare for minors under 19; upheld against one-subject challenge after being attached to abortion bill
leads.detail: Passed Legislature May 2023 by 33-15 vote, signed by Governor Jim Pillen effective immediately; upheld by Nebraska Supreme Court 6-1 in July 2024

leads.title: Obergefell v. Hodges / Attorney General Doug Peterson compliance statement and Waters v. Ricketts
leads.documents: Legal status of same-sex marriage in Nebraska; state will not enforce laws contrary to Obergefell
leads.detail: U.S. Supreme Court decided June 26, 2015; AG statement same day: 'State of Nebraska will comply'; Waters v. Ricketts, U.S. District Court for District of Nebraska struck down constitutional ban, listed in External links as March 2, 2015

leads.title: Nebraska hate crime statute (1997) and State Supreme Court April 2016 Duncan decision
leads.documents: Hate-crime enforcement machinery covering sexual orientation; documented Old Market Omaha incident where straight victim with gay friends was attacked
leads.detail: Statute protects right to live free from violence regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, or disability; October 2013 attack by Gregory Duncan on Ryan Langenegger; conviction for third-degree assault + hate crime upheld April 2016

leads.title: Omaha city ordinance (2012) and Lincoln actions
leads.documents: Local anti-discrimination rights machinery for employment, public accommodations, and housing
leads.detail: Omaha ordinance in effect since 2012 prohibits discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in employment and public accommodations; Lincoln City Council passed 5-0 February 2022 ordinance for employment, accommodation and housing, removed June 2022 after Nebraska Family Alliance petition drive; Lincoln conversion therapy ban since 2021

leads.title: Stewart v. Heineman / Nebraska Supreme Court April 2017 foster-parent decision and March 2021 adoption decision
leads.documents: Court rulings striking Nebraska bans on same-sex couples as foster and adoptive parents
leads.detail: Lancaster County District Judge John Colborn ruled for plaintiffs August 5, 2015; Nebraska Supreme Court upheld April 2017 comparing law to 'a sign reading Whites Only'; Nebraska Supreme Court March 2021 reversed lower court to allow same-sex married couple to adopt
